wholeCurrentGoal.title: Genommutationen durch Meiosefehler erklären
wholeCurrentGoal.titleEn: Explain Genome Mutations Caused by Meiotic Errors
wholeCurrentGoal.description: Die lernende Person kann Genommutationen beim Menschen als Folge von Fehlern bei der Meiose erklären.
wholeCurrentGoal.descriptionEn: The learner can explain human genome mutations as consequences of errors during meiosis.

Display-width inspection derivative only; no author asset edit or production

images.scientificMechanism: Two duplicated homologous chromosome21 symbols enter the same MI daughter; the other lacks chromosome21. Normal MII separates their sister chromatids, giving two gametes with two chromosome21 copies and two with none.
images.scientificFormAndGeometry: The blue/red X symbols persist together only after MI; four final cells correctly contain two single-chromatid rods or no chromosome21. The heading Chromosom21 bounds the blank-cell depiction to that chromosome, rather than depicting chromosome-free human gametes.
images.phoneReadability: At360 all four principal labels and the chromosome symbols/arrows are clear. Large model objects show the error without needing a small legend.
images.desktopAndOriginalReadability: At680 and original the centromeres, X/rod distinction, branching arrows and model scope are readily visible.
images.actorAndOutsideViewerPerspective: No actor-held directional object; this is a diagram for the outside viewer.
images.comicFormatAgeAndGoalFit: Friendly rounded cell/chromosome schematic is appropriate for SekI/introductory human meiosis and preserves the orientation function.
images.orientationAndEvidenceLimit: Only chromosome21 is shown; no actual gamete, patient, experiment or diagnosis is inferred.

wholeCurrentGoal.title: Phänotypänderung und Krankheit bei Genommutationen unterscheiden
wholeCurrentGoal.titleEn: Distinguish Phenotypic Change and Disease in Genome Mutations
wholeCurrentGoal.description: Die lernende Person kann im Kontext von Genommutationen zwischen einer Änderung des Phänotyps und einer Krankheit unterscheiden.
wholeCurrentGoal.descriptionEn: The learner can distinguish between phenotypic change and disease in the context of genome mutations.

images.scientificMechanism: Chromosome findings, a visible trait and additional functional/health findings are separated into three panels. The question mark on the dashed relation prevents automatic disease inference.
images.scientificFormAndGeometry: The magnifying-glass chromosome symbols are a generic schematic, not a numbered or claimed full karyotype. The heart/clipboard icons refer to independent health findings. Neither drawn learner is assigned a specific mutation or disease.
images.phoneReadability: At360 the three headings, question mark and the two-line separation sentence remain readable. The small Zusatzbefunde/Körperfunktionen lettering is secondary to the readable main distinction.
images.desktopAndOriginalReadability: At680 the health icons and Zusatzbefunde label are clear and the footer can be read without zooming.
images.actorAndOutsideViewerPerspective: Clipboard is a front-facing explanatory poster object; neither character is shown reading an inverted document. The eye/magnifier is a trait-observation icon.
images.comicFormatAgeAndGoalFit: Respectful comic learners and distinct blue/yellow/green panels are approachable; appearance is not presented as a diagnosis.
images.orientationAndEvidenceLimit: The characters are illustration, not real patient or learner evidence; the drawing does not establish a genotype for either person.

wholeCurrentGoal.title: DNA- und RNA-Strukturmodelle vergleichen
wholeCurrentGoal.titleEn: Compare DNA and RNA Structure Models
wholeCurrentGoal.description: Die lernende Person kann ein Modell zum Bau der DNA beschreiben und mit einem entsprechenden Modell zum Bau der RNA vergleichen.
wholeCurrentGoal.descriptionEn: The learner can describe a model of DNA structure and compare it with a corresponding model of RNA structure.

inspectionDerivatives.role: Display-width inspection derivative only; no author asset edit or production
Display-width inspection derivative only; no author asset edit or production

images.scientificMechanism: DNA is shown as complementary antiparallel paired chains with A–T and G–C; the RNA example has a single sugar-phosphate chain with U. D/R distinguish the supplied sugar schematics.
images.scientificFormAndGeometry: A–T/T–A show two interbase dashes; G–C/C–G show three. The two DNA arrows point in opposite directions. Backbone connections are solid and interbase links dashed.
images.phoneReadability: At360 the bases, D/R sugars, double versus single chain and opposed arrows are distinct; the necessary labels DNA/RNA remain large.
images.desktopAndOriginalReadability: At680 and original the dashed bond counts and continuous backbones are clear.
images.actorAndOutsideViewerPerspective: No actor or directional reading surface; antiparallel chain direction is a viewer-facing diagram relation.
images.comicFormatAgeAndGoalFit: Large colored molecular tokens meet the need to compare simplified structure models without a sterile atomic diagram.
images.orientationAndEvidenceLimit: This is a typical simplified RNA example, not a claim that all RNA is single-stranded or that D/R constitute a full chemical structural formula.

wholeCurrentGoal.title: Genetischen Code in beide Richtungen anwenden
wholeCurrentGoal.titleEn: Apply the Genetic Code in Both Directions
wholeCurrentGoal.description: Die lernende Person kann aus DNA-Basensequenzen Aminosäuresequenzen ableiten und aus Aminosäuresequenzen mögliche codierende DNA-Basensequenzen rekonstruieren, indem sie den genetischen Code anwendet.
wholeCurrentGoal.descriptionEn: The learner can derive amino acid sequences from DNA base sequences and reconstruct possible coding DNA sequences from amino acid sequences by applying the genetic code.

Display-width inspection derivative only; no author asset edit or production

images.scientificMechanism: Two coding-sequence examples ATG GAA and ATG GAG lead to AUG GAA/AUG GAG and both Met–Glu. Yellow reconstruction arrows return to two possible DNA examples under the visible Mehrere Möglichkeiten heading.
images.scientificFormAndGeometry: The sequence letters and codon mapping are correct under coding-strand/left-to-right reading. The reverse arrows are a learner reconstruction relation, not a depicted biochemical protein-to-DNA synthesis pathway.
images.phoneReadability: At360 DNA/mRNA, both codon strings, Met–Glu and Mehrere Möglichkeiten are large enough to read. Color-separated arrows retain forward versus reconstruction directions.
images.desktopAndOriginalReadability: At680 the two alternatives and the green converging arrows are clear; the gold reverse arrows terminate at the two DNA panels.
images.actorAndOutsideViewerPerspective: The student looks toward the diagram; the open book has decorative lines and no inverted meaningful text. The pen/hand pose is plausible.
images.comicFormatAgeAndGoalFit: Comic learner plus simple mapping panels support the bidirectional code goal without pretending the raster is a full64-codon lookup instrument.
images.orientationAndEvidenceLimit: Coding strand/orientation assumptions need to remain in the bound teaching text. No stop codon or full protein function is claimed for the two-residue fragment.

wholeCurrentGoal.titleEn: Explain Protein Biosynthesis and Its Significance for Life
wholeCurrentGoal.description: Die lernende Person kann den Mechanismus der Proteinbiosynthese beschreiben und die Bedeutung der Proteinbildung für Lebewesen erklären.
wholeCurrentGoal.descriptionEn: The learner can describe the mechanism of protein biosynthesis and explain the significance of protein formation for living organisms.

images.scientificMechanism: Bacterial DNA/mRNA/ribosome/tRNA and nuclear transcription/export through a visible pore to cytoplasmic translation are correctly distinguished at overview level. Lower icons illustrate catalytic, structural, transport and defense roles.
images.scientificFormAndGeometry: The eukaryotic mRNA visibly crosses the nuclear boundary at a drawn pore; the ribosome is outside. Charged tRNA arrows approach ribosomes and protein chains leave. This is not a claim of simultaneous bacterial coupling or a full molecular enzyme equation.
images.phoneReadability: HOLD: at360 the required mechanism labels mRNA/tRNA/Ribosom/Kernpore and the function labels/explanatory lines are reduced to roughly5–7 pixels or less. Headings remain clear, but essential detailed stages/functions cannot be reliably read at the intended phone size.
images.desktopAndOriginalReadability: At680 and original the same labels and flow are readable. The failure is the actual phone composition density, not PNG dimensions or an unviewed hash.
images.actorAndOutsideViewerPerspective: No actor or instrument using a reversed surface; cell interiors are conceptual cutaways.
images.comicFormatAgeAndGoalFit: Friendly cells and protein-function icons fit the visual language, but the two-cell plus four-function layout is too dense at360.
images.orientationAndEvidenceLimit: The lower enzyme tokens are schematic rather than a stoichiometric equation; do not use the icon count as quantitative reaction evidence.

wholeCurrentGoal.title: Alternatives Spleißen für Proteinvielfalt erklären
wholeCurrentGoal.titleEn: Explain Alternative Splicing for Protein Diversity

wholeCurrentGoal.descriptionEn: The learner can explain how alternative splicing increases protein diversity in eukaryotes and contextualize it as a prerequisite for evolutionary selection processes.

images.scientificMechanism: A pre-mRNA from one gene has E1/E2/E3/E4 and intervening introns. Mature E1–E2–E4 versus E1–E3–E4 produces two color-consistent protein variants under the supplied exon-compatibility model.
images.scientificFormAndGeometry: Shared E1/E4 and mutually selected E2/E3 are retained consistently in mature RNA and corresponding domain-color illustrations; intron connectors disappear. No evolutionary selection arrow or inheritance claim appears in the raster.

images.desktopAndOriginalReadability: At680 the pre-/mature-RNA labels and removed intervening segments are clear.
images.actorAndOutsideViewerPerspective: No actor; all token order and process arrows are coherent for the outside viewer.
images.comicFormatAgeAndGoalFit: Large rounded exon/protein icons suit the molecular model; this is a bounded isoform illustration.
images.orientationAndEvidenceLimit: Raster PASS does not close the separately sealed whole-goal DE/EN prerequisite-claim finding BIO23-A-001. No inevitable selection, stable inheritance or actual protein-folding prediction is proved.
